title: Calibrate current Astra on a strict complete API build before planner experiments
hypothesis: A complete local API build exercises enough current-model planning, verification and recovery to serve as a useful longer-task speed workload.
falsified_if: The strict grader is invalid or current Astra completes the task without the long trajectory properties being studied; do not call a small-tool run a long coding task.
local_evidence: Historical auth_api runs included 20+ tools and repairs, but used older prompts and repeated planner updates. A new strict scenario requires all existing behavioral probes and completed final unittest evidence, preserving historical grading. Offline replay shows a plaintext-token mutation passes the old score (95) but fails the new mandatory security gate.
deterministic_outcomes: protected README and no unrelated infrastructure
efficiency_outcomes: all-attempt task latency and estimated cost
decision_rule: Seed 916. Two independent smoke runs: simple_prompt and auth_api_strict. Then four pilot runs: both scenarios, two repetitions, one baseline arm. At most six launches, $8 between-run standard-equivalent cost threshold (one-run overshoot possible), 1500 active worker seconds. No retries or failed-run exclusion; halt on smoke or protocol/activation failures. This is workload calibration, not a causal speed claim. Record all three API builds including smoke, and distinguish pilot statistics. A candidate long-workload label requires at least two of three API trajectories to use 20+ actual tools, touch multiple code files, and show genuine failed verification/revision or a changed investigated assumption; do not force extra tool operations to satisfy the label. Count actual current planner calls and standalone planner turns before designing a no-planner treatment. If calibration is too short or unreliable, retain evidence and build a richer workload rather than asserting a planner speed improvement. No default changes.
